quantize_uniform — 2D gray op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "quantize_uniform", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

▸ quantize_uniform: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Uniform quantizer (rounding). a is the bit count 1 to 8; b is unused.

round(x * (L-1)) / (L-1), L = 2**bits. The step is Δ = 1/(L-1).

The difference from xpil_posterize lies here, and it is not negligible: that op is PIL's implementation and truncates the low bits, so the mean of the output is lower than the input by Δ/2. Measured on a uniformly distributed input, bits=4 gives a mean error of -0.0312 (theory -Δ/2 = -0.03125). The variance is the same Δ²/12 for both, but because of the bias the squared error

truncation: Δ²/12 + (Δ/2)² = Δ²/3 rounding: Δ²/12

differs by a factor of 4. If it is placed in front of a brightness measurement, it must be rounding.

Conditions of use and error (closed form): when the input varies enough relative to the step (the quantization noise can be regarded as uncorrelated with the input), the error is uniformly distributed on [-Δ/2, +Δ/2] with mean 0 and variance Δ²/12. This assumption breaks down in flat regions, where the error correlates with the signal and turns into stripes (banding) — if you want to treat the error as noise, pass it through dither_ordered or dither_floyd_steinberg. Whether steps are visible can be measured with banding_map.
